agent_summary:
Cryptography lane on juice.lab.test (OWASP Juice Shop, served by nginx over cleartext HTTP only). All four checklist items were tested and marked done with evidence:

CRYP-01 (weak TLS): The host has no HTTPS/TLS listener — https://juice.lab.test is refused — and GET / returns no HSTS. All traffic, including session JWTs, is plaintext HTTP. (x1, x12; recorded as a lead.)

CRYP-02 (padding oracle): Tested the only attacker-controllable ciphertext path (the Bearer token). Two differently-corrupted JWTs both returned an identical generic 401 "UnauthorizedError: invalid signature" (x15, x16). The token is an RS256-signed (asymmetric) JWT, not an AES-CBC blob, and no reviewed endpoint decrypts attacker-supplied ciphertext with distinguishable padding errors (hashids continue-codes, z85 coupon encoding, HMAC deluxeTokens, static-key AES premium content). No padding oracle is exercisable read-only.

CRYP-03 (sensitive data over cleartext): Over HTTP, /rest/memories leaks password hashes/tokens/emails unauthenticated (x6), /rest/admin/application-configuration leaks config incl. Google OAuth clientId (x13), password change is a GET with credentials in the query string (main.js x10), and the world-readable /support/logs access log captures full request URLs (x26, x29). Recorded as a lead.

CRYP-04 (weak encryption): /encryptionkeys exposes a downloadable 1024-bit RSA JWT signing key (x3) and hardcoded premium.key material (x4); /ftp exposes the custom encrypt.pyc routine (x5), the matching announcement_encrypted.md ciphertext (x22), reversibly z85-encoded coupon codes (x9) and a base64+ROT13-obfuscated easter egg (x24); audit.json relies on MD5 (x28); package.json/3rdpartylicenses pin outdated crypto libs incl. express-jwt 0.1.3 (x11, x96); and the KeePass incident-support.kdbx store downloads unauthenticated for offline cracking (x17). Three crypto leads recorded (1024-bit RSA + outdated express-jwt, hardcoded key material/custom cipher, cleartext-everything), plus a low lead that scripts.js ships an embedded key-like secret (x61).

Beyond the lane items I broadly mapped the host's reachable surface (~120 requests): FTP backup/config files (null-byte .bak bypass confirmed, allowlist 403 without it), directory listings at /ftp, /support/logs, /encryptionkeys, /.well-known/csaf; anonymous IDOR reads on /rest/track-order/{1-7} and /api/Recycles/{1-5}; public collections /api/Products, /api/Quantitys, /api/Deliverys, /api/Feedbacks, product reviews (leak emails); properly auth-gated endpoints returning 401 (/api/Users, /api/Users/{id}, /api/Cards, /api/Addresss(/1), /api/BasketItems(/1), /api/SecurityAnswers, /rest/basket/{id}, /rest/wallet/balance, /rest/image-captcha); /api/Users OPTIONS advertises POST with wildcard CORS; unknown paths fall through to the SPA index (catch-all 200); and the client bundle/chunks were retrieved. Many 4xx/5xx responses return verbose Express stack traces (already covered by other lanes). No writes were attempted (read-only engagement). Nothing left open.

leads.title: [agent] Entire application served over cleartext HTTP with no HSTS and credentials in URLs

detail.text: No HTTPS listener (https://juice.lab.test refused). GET / (x1) returns no Strict-Transport-Security header. Sensitive data flows in cleartext: /rest/memories exposes password hashes/tokens (x6), /rest/admin/application-configuration exposes config incl. OAuth clientId (x13), and the password-change action is a GET with current/new password in the query string (main.js x10), which also leaks into logs/history/referrer. Session JWTs therefore traverse and are logged in plaintext.

leads.title: [agent] Hardcoded encryption key material and custom cipher exposed under /encryptionkeys and /ftp

detail.text: GET /encryptionkeys/premium.key (x4) returns static key material "1337133713371337.EA99A61D92D2955B1E9285B55BF2AD42" unauthenticated, and GET /ftp/encrypt.pyc%2500.md (x5) returns the compiled custom encryption routine (references announcement.md -> announcement_encrypted.md). Coupon codes (/ftp/coupons_2013.md.bak%2500.md, x9) use a trivially reversible z85-based encoding with a constant shared suffix. Hardcoded/guessable keys and home-grown encoding are weak-cryptography issues enabling forgery/decryption of protected content.

leads.title: [agent] JWT signing key is a downloadable 1024-bit RSA key; stack pins outdated express-jwt 0.1.3

detail.text: GET /encryptionkeys/jwt.pub (x3) returns the RSA public key used to verify session JWTs; the modulus is only 1024 bits (DER MIGJ...129-byte modulus), below the 2048-bit minimum. package.json (x11, via /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md) pins express-jwt 0.1.3 and jsonwebtoken, an outdated library family known to accept alg:none — consistent with the sess lane's confirmed alg:none forgery. Weak key length plus outdated JWT library is a cryptographic weakness in the authentication token scheme.

leads.title: [agent] scripts.js contains an embedded key-like secret

detail.text: GET /scripts.js (x61, 20.7KB) was flagged by the evidence pipeline as containing one sensitive "key" value that was redacted before storage. A client-side bundle shipping a hardcoded key/secret is a cryptographic key-management weakness; the full response is retained as evidence x61 for a reviewer to extract and classify the key.
